nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the equation T relate to the components of the supply chain model?
nodes.answer: The equation T relates to the cycle time and circularity index, which are essential components for optimizing profits in the supply chain model.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Circular supply chains_qna_001
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the algorithm determine the optimal cycle time value and circularity index in the three-layer coordinated supply chain system?
nodes.answer: The algorithm considers the values of T and AWAY corresponding to the highest total profit, which are then identified as the optimal cycle time value T* and circularity index AWAY*.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Circular supply chains_qna_002
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What was the optimal cycle time and circularity index for the supplier in the textile industry?
nodes.answer: The optimal cycle time was T = 2.86,465 and the optimal circularity index AWAY = 0.774,982 for the supplier in the textile industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Circular supply chains_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the two research questions addressed in the study?
nodes.answer: The two research questions are: (1) What circular loops and aspects are addressed when digital technologies are integrated in the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? (2) Which trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle?

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Circular supply chains_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the challenges involved in redesigning traditional linear supply chains into circular supply chains as discussed by Roy et al. (2022)?
nodes.answer: Roy et al. (2022) highlight the challenges in redesigning traditional linear supply chains into circular supply chains, such as overcoming entrenched practices, adapting to new technologies, and managing the complexities of reverse logistics and product recovery.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Circular economy practices|Circular supply chains_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are the drivers, barriers, and practices towards circular economy from a supply chain perspective according to a systematic review?
nodes.answer: According to a systematic review, the drivers, barriers, and practices towards circular economy from a supply chain perspective include factors such as resource scarcity, regulatory requirements, innovation opportunities, and collaboration with stakeholders.
